title: Throughput Remediation & Credit Escalation Framework (TREC)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview:
This ticket defines an end-to-end framework for measuring dedicated capacity throughput degradations, computing error-budget-backed credits, and escalating remediation steps (auto-scaling, prioritized burst, and financial crediting). The goal is a deterministic, auditable contract flow customers can rely on and sales/legal can commit to in renewals and SOWs.

SLA metric definition (summary):
- Primary metric: Serve-throughput availability defined as the fraction of successful token-serve capacity within customer-entitled throughput window. Measured as: 1 - (sum of deficit_tokens / entitlement_tokens) over the rolling 30-day window, computed from per-5min windows.
- Thresholds: Gold: >= 99.7%, Silver: >= 99.0%, Bronze: >= 95.0%.
- Measurement window: per-5min sampling, aggregated hourly, then quantile-smoothed over 30 days to avoid noise from single-minute spikes.

Error budget & credit calculus (proposed):
- Error budget is computed as entitlement_tokens * (1 - SLA_target) for the 30-day window.
- Credit buckets: proportional credits are assigned by severity band (Gold/Silver/Bronze) and duration. Short-term transient (<6 hours) gets operational remediation and engineering review; multi-hour sustained deficits trigger proportional credits.
- Example formula (plain language): if customer entitlement is 1M tokens/day and monthly SLA shortfall is 0.5% over 30 days, credit = proportional_share_of_monthly_fee * (shortfall_percent / SLA_tolerance). Exact numeric multiplier table included in attachments.

Escalation ladder (operational & contract):
1) Auto-remediation: autoscaler policy attempts to add burst capacity (per-customer burst pool) within 120s.
2) Priority routing: route traffic to standby model variant or AZ if capacity available within 5 minutes.
3) Proportional credits: once degradation exceeds 3x the per-day error budget or persists >4 hours, apply financial credit per the formula.
4) Review & cure: sustained or repeated failures escalate to on-call + account team + legal notification.
5) Reserved-capacity remediation: for Dedicated customers, if platform is causally responsible, credit is applied and a remediation timeline is committed (72 hours to restore to baseline or further credits).

Contract language guidance (legal-friendly snippets):
- "Service Level" definition: "The Service Level for Dedicated Throughput is the percentage of entitled token serving capacity successfully fulfilled by Redwood Inference within the measurement window, as measured by Redwood's monitoring systems."
- "Credit entitlement": "If Redwood fails to meet the Service Level for a given calendar month, Customer shall be eligible to receive Service Credits calculated in accordance with the Credit Table in Appendix A. Credits are Customer's exclusive monetary remedy for service level failures."
- Notice & cure: "Customer must notify Redwood within 21 days of the performance incident. Redwood will investigate and provide a remediation plan within 72 hours of notification."

Measurement & telemetry:
- Required signals: per-tenant token counts, kernel-scheduling rejections, queue-length percentiles, and autoscale actions.
- Aggregation: compute per-5min deficit = max(0, entitlement_tokens - served_tokens). Persist raw per-5min metrics for 90 days for audits.
- Reporting: weekly SLO dashboard and automated monthly credit calculations exposed to customers via Console.

Operational playbooks & links:
- Runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Dedicated+Throughput+Remediation (work-in-progress).
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls/3892 (autoscaler: per-tenant burst pool), github.com/redwood-inference/metrics/pulls/241 (SLA aggregation logic).

Open decisions & trade-offs: 
- Measurement smoothing: whether to use 95th percentile of hourly aggregates vs. quantile smoothing of 30-day series. Trade-off: sensitivity to short spikes vs. slower detection for sustained degradations.
- Credit granularity: per-day credits vs. monthly aggregated crediting. Ops prefers per-incident credits for faster remediation; Finance prefers monthly aggregation to limit churn.
- Burst pool funding: should burst pools be metered and chargeable when used? Requires pricing discussion with GTM.

Acceptance criteria:
- Draft contract text vetted by Legal and Sales (Sofia Nguyen sign-off).
- Implementation ticket for SLA aggregation and crediting in metrics pipeline (ENG-19876) confirmed and has integration tests.
- Console displays the monthly credit calculation and historical per-5min deficit graph for customer accounts.

Attachments (links):
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/TREC+Draft
- Example credit table (CSV): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/pm/trec-credit-table.csv
- Related RFC: https://rfc.redwood.ai/rfc/dedicated-throughput-remediation-2026

Notes:
- I intentionally separated operational remediation (autoscale, routing) from contractual remediation (credits, notice/cure) to keep SLAs auditable and reduce dispute surface area.
- We should aim for a minimal set of quantifiable metrics in the contract and push complex diagnostics into the Console and runbooks.
